detail.title: Music Perception as Predictive Processing: Synthesis of ASAP Hypothesis and Interoceptive Inference
detail.summary: This journal entry synthesizes research into how musical structures engage the brain's predictive processing systems. The ASAP hypothesis (Action Simulation for Auditory Prediction) suggests that music perception involves motor simulation to track rhythmic sequences. Complementary research on interoceptive inference frames music-induced emotion as a 'controlled hallucination,' where the brain anticipates sensory outcomes and calibrates its internal state accordingly. Together, these frameworks support the view that musical pleasure arises from the resolution—or expected violation—of predictive models.
